industry_scenarios.title: Load, deliver, collect and settle one van
steps: Load 40 snack cases and 50 water cases.
Deliver 30 cases of each across two stops; accept two returned water cases.
Return 10 snack cases and 22 water cases to the warehouse.
Reconcile cash sale 360, bank deposit 200 and retained cash 160 separately from bank-transfer receipts.
acceptance_checks: Location transfers do not change company-wide inventory or profit.
Credit invoices are receivables, not collected route cash.
No routing, location tracking or offline operation is implemented.

scenario.title: Follow a distribution route settlement
scenario.goal: Review a distributor's stock, customer invoice, supplier bill, settlement and route-level bookkeeping evidence.
steps: Review the opening stock, customer receivable and supplier payable evidence.
Trace stock receipt and a credit sale through inventory, cost and control accounts.
Apply the named customer and supplier settlements and inspect residuals.
Review the route and cash-transfer notes as bookkeeping references only.
checks: The distribution scenario does not implement route planning, dispatch, delivery proof or fleet accounting.
Inventory uses one location and the shared moving-average service.
Customer and supplier settlement remains separate from operational delivery status.

notice: Original sample general-ledger examples. Manual staff, loan, outstanding-item and stock schedules do not implement payroll, AR/AP, inventory or tax modules. Period closure blocks posting; it is not statutory financial-statement approval or an earnings-transfer journal.

company_profile.tax_registrations: Sample registration SAMPLE-TRN-0000000. Invented for this demonstration; it is not a real tax registration and no country tax rule is applied.
company_profile.footer_terms: Payment due 30 days from the invoice date. Goods remain the property of the seller until paid in full. Every figure, party and registration on this document belongs to a fictional demonstration company.

anticipated_1_3.notice: Authored so the 1.3 features below have real history to act on the day they land. None of this is produced by a screen, a register or a scheduler in 1.2.0; every figure here was posted by an ordinary journal in the history above.

deferred_income.instrument: Annual support plan collected in advance

asset_register.convention: A full month in the month an asset enters service, and none in the month it is disposed of
asset_register.note: The 1.3 fixed-assets module posts an acquisition, each period's depreciation and a disposal itself. Replaying this block through it needs a pack-format asset section and an importer step; until that exists the journals above carry the same figures.

loan_schedule.note: Two instalments are posted in the history. The remaining three are schedule data only; nothing generates them today.

year_end.note: The 2025 periods are closed, which blocks backdated posting. No closing journal has been posted and no year is locked: 1.2.0 has neither, and the balances above are what a year-end close would have to work from.

period_close.note: There is no reverse-on flag and no cash-count document in 1.2.0; these name the history a close checklist would ask about.
